cultural_notes: Duluth sits on Lake Superior, the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area; the Aerial Lift Bridge and the working ore port define the waterfront (source: en.wikipedia.org Duluth, Minnesota; Aerial Lift Bridge)

the North Shore, Boundary Waters, and Superior National Forest make this a big-lake and wilderness outdoor market -- canoe, hike, and cabin culture (source: general North Woods framing, publicly documented)

Lake Superior is called Gitchi-Gami in Ojibwe; the region has deep Ojibwe (Anishinaabe) heritage -- reference respectfully, no tribal endorsement implied without consent (source: general framing; Ojibwe place-name note)

wild blueberries grow across the North Woods and are foraged and sold locally in summer; Cub Foods, Super One Foods, and the Whole Foods Co-op are the grocers (source: chain regional footprint; wild-blueberry regional framing)
